policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads "by every prophet, and every seer" with no possessive: the qere construct nebi'e stands in apposition to kol-hozeh and is rendered as two coordinate items. The ketiv nebi'o carries a third-person suffix ("his prophet"), which the ASV does not render here, though it renders possessives elsewhere in the verse ("my servants the prophets"). ASV wording distinguishes the qere.

Qere shene (construct) and ketiv shenayim (absolute) both yield "two calves" in English; the difference is Hebrew state, which no English wording can show. No ASV note is mapped to this unit. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

ASV text reads "Jeroboam drove Israel from following Jehovah", rendering the qere wayyaddah (nadah, drive away), and the mapped note "According to another reading, drew Israel away" explicitly relegates the ketiv wayyadde' to the margin as another reading. The text renders the base; the note names the alternative as not adopted.

ASV text reads "the gods of Sepharvaim", plural, matching the qere 'elohe; the ketiv 'elah is singular and would give "the god of". The note "Or, god" is classed alternative_rendering and does not decide the reading, but the plural in the ASV text itself distinguishes the qere.

ASV transliterates "Sepharvaim", reproducing the qere sepharvayim consonant for consonant; the ketiv sepharim would have yielded "Sepharim", as it does not contain the vav-yod of the ASV form. The ASV spelling of the proper name distinguishes the qere.
